# glyhub <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="glyhub logo" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

glyhub aims to provide a curated collection of glycomics and glycoproteomics
datasets from the literature and public databases. The planned collection will
store datasets as `GlycomicSE` and `GlycoproteomicSE` objects from
[glyexp](https://github.com/glycoverse/glyexp), bringing measurements, molecular
annotations, and sample metadata together in a consistent format.

## Development status

**glyhub is currently a package skeleton.** It does not yet include curated
datasets or data-access functions. Dataset examples will be added when the first
resources are available.

The initial design is to bundle curated datasets with the package and make them
available through R's `LazyData` mechanism. This is a planned architecture;
datasets, the dependency on glyexp, and lazy loading have not yet been implemented.

## Installation

You can install the development skeleton from
[GitHub](https://github.com/glycoverse/glyhub):

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("glycoverse/glyhub")
```

Installing the current skeleton does not provide any datasets.

## Role in `glycoverse`

The intended role of glyhub is to collect and curate reusable experimental data
for the Glycoverse ecosystem. glyexp provides the `GlycomicSE` and
`GlycoproteomicSE` containers; glyhub is planned to supply curated datasets stored
in those containers for examples, method development, and reproducible analyses.
